title: Milestones
theme: A new job, moving out, a birthday, a farewell, someone new arriving.

storylets.title: A candle in a bun
storylets.note: A small birthday at a stall. Age appears only if somebody says it.

B.desc: a friend with a bun and a candle

b1: {A} sits at a stool and scrolls a handset with one eyebrow up.
{A} takes a stool and drums fingers on the counter.
{A} perches on a stool and looks across the square.
b2: {B.desc} arrives and sets a bun with a single candle in front of {A}.
{B.desc} hands {A} a small wrapped bun with a lit candle on top.
{B.desc} holds out a paper plate with a sparkler stuck in a dumpling.
b3: {A} blows the candle out, laughs, and the two of them hug.
{B.desc} wraps {A} in a hug while the candle gutters.
{A} grabs {B.desc} in a hug that nearly tips the plate.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Forty! Make a wish, you old thing."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Twenty-five today. Eat the bun before I do."
Overheard: {A} says: "Best friend I ever had, remembering the day."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Of course I remembered, friend. Who else would?"

storylets.title: A bag at the metro mouth
storylets.note: Someone leaves the city. The watcher sees the goodbye; afterward the person stays in the notebook, read-only and past tense (rule 11).

A.desc: an adult leaving with a bag

b1: {A} and {B.desc} walk to the station entrance, {A} dragging a heavy bag.
{B.desc} carries half of {A}'s load as the two reach the stairs.
{A} and {B.desc} cross the plaza slowly, saying little.
b2: {A} and {B.desc} hug for a long time at the top of the steps.
{B.desc} holds on to {A} until the platform bell rings.
{A} and {B.desc} embrace and neither lets go first.
b3: {A} goes down alone and boards. The train pulls out.
{A} rides down and the doors hiss shut on a last wave.
{A} takes the train and does not look back.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "I'll write when I'm settled. Don't wait up on me."
Overheard: {A} says: "They gave me a place upriver. I leave tonight."

lines: Overheard: {S} tells {L} that {A.desc} left the city on the evening train. Just a bag and a coat.
Overheard: {S} says to {L}: "{A.desc} is gone. Took the metro out and did not say where."
Overheard: {S} says {A.desc} has moved away from the city for good.
Overheard: {S} mentions to {L} that {A.desc} left last week and sent a card.
entry: Left the city last week (overheard: a neighbor, in conversation).
Took the train out for good, per {S} (overheard, in conversation).
Moved away from the district, said {S} (overheard).

storylets.title: A badge for the first morning
storylets.note: Follows wrk.found-new-job. The new worker stands at a door holding a fresh badge.

A.desc: a newcomer at a work door

b1: {A} stands at the work door with a fresh badge on a spotless jacket.
{A} waits outside the workplace, turning a badge over and over.
{A} arrives early and stays at the door with a thermos.
b2: {B.desc} comes out and shakes {A}'s hand, then points up at the lights.
{B.desc} says a few words and {A} nods hard to each.
{B.desc} hands {A} a sheet of printed rules and explains the first hour.
b3: {B.desc} leads {A} in. The door slides shut behind them.
{A} follows {B.desc} through the door with the badge held out.
Both go in. {A} looks back once at the street.

log: The badge reads Floor Assistant, first week.

storylets.title: A small box on the bench
storylets.note: A proposal. Rare, brief, public by accident. Whether it is accepted is shown by what happens next.

A.desc: an adult holding a small box

b1: {A} and {B.desc} sit side by side. {A} is very still and keeps a hand in a pocket.
{A} and {B.desc} take a bench by the pond. {A} fidgets with a zipper.
{B.desc} sits and {A} sits stiff beside, one knee jumping.
b2: {A} takes a small box from a pocket and holds it out in both hands.
{A} hands {B.desc} a small box and says a few words.
{A} holds out a flat box. {B.desc} stares at it, then at {A}.
b3: {B.desc} throws both arms around {A} and the box falls on the bench.
{A} and {B.desc} embrace. A passerby claps.
{B.desc} hugs {A} hard and says something into {A}'s shoulder.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "You've been my {B.rel} eight years. I'd like eight more. Marry me."
Overheard: {A} says: "My {B.rel}, my best friend. Will you marry me?"
Overheard: {A} says: "Will you marry me? I know it's a bench. I couldn't wait for a better one."

storylets.title: Carrying a frame home
storylets.note: A framed certificate carried through the square. A graduation or a license, left unsaid.

A.desc: an adult carrying a flat frame

b1: {A} carries a flat frame wrapped in paper, held out in front like a tray.
{A} walks the block with a framed sheet under one arm, keeping clear of the crowd.
{A} hugs a framed document to the chest and steps over puddles.
b2: {A} points at the frame, then at the sky, and says something to a passerby.
{A} shows the corner of the frame to a stall keeper with a small bow.
{A} gestures toward the frame and a stranger nods approvingly.
b3: {A} goes in and the door slides shut on the paper.
{A} enters, holding the frame high over the threshold.
{A} steps inside and the door closes.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "Three years of night classes. They gave me this today."
Overheard: {A} says: "It says I'm licensed. Licensed! Look at that stamp."

storylets.title: The box and the handshakes
storylets.note: A long-serving worker leaves for the last time. A small crowd at the work door.

A.desc: an older worker leaving a workplace

b1: {A} comes out of the work door with a small box and a plant in the crook of an arm.
{A} leaves the workplace with a cake box held level.
{A} steps out of the work door to scattered applause.
b2: {B.desc} and {A} hug at the door. A few others wait their turn.
{A} embraces {B.desc} and then shakes the next hand.
{B.desc} hugs {A} and says a few words that make {A} laugh.
b3: {A} walks away down the block, the plant held high.
{A} heads off with a slow stride, not looking back.
{A} crosses the square with the box on a hip.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Thirty-one years. Nobody will remember where anything is."
Overheard: {A} says: "I'm leaving the keys on the hook. Don't lose them."

storylets.title: A flower on a bench slat
storylets.note: Someone leaves a flower where another used to sit. Never explained; never needs to be.

b1: {A} walks up to a bench with a single stem in one hand.
{A} approaches the bench with eyes lowered.
{A} crosses to the bench and stops at its end.
b2: {A} lays the flower along the bench slats and lifts a withered one from the arm.
{A} replaces an old bloom with the new one and tucks the old one in a pocket.
{A} brushes the slats clear with a sleeve.
b3: {A} stands at the bench for several minutes, hands folded.
{A} stays beside the bench, head bowed, until the bell rings.
{A} lingers, touching the slats once, then walks away.

log: Overheard: {A} says to the bench: "I'll be back on the fifteenth. Same time."
Overheard: {A} says: "This was your seat. I kept it clean."

storylets.title: Posted with a tiny shoe
storylets.note: News reaches the monitor only as a post. The feed says what the person chose to say.

b1: {A} sits on a bench holding a handset close and grinning at the screen.
{A} takes a seat and shows the handset to nobody in particular.
{A} perches on the bench edge, thumbing the screen with great care.
b2: {A} posts a picture, reads the comment that appears, and laughs out loud.
{A} posts a single line and holds the handset to the chest.
{A} types, deletes, types, and finally posts.

log: Posted: "She arrived at dawn. Seven pounds, loud, perfect. Visiting hours start tomorrow."
Posted: "New to the family: a small person with strong opinions. Everyone is fine."
